\section[o futuro]{o futuro — the future}

\label{lesson:PT-C136-o-futuro}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the past, then the Portuguese for to happen.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o futuro}
\textbf{o futuro} — \textquotedblleft{}the future\textquotedblright{}. Portuguese has two futures. The everyday one is \textbf{ir} with an infinitive: \textbf{Vou falar.} — \textquotedblleft{}I am going to speak.\textquotedblright{} The one-word future adds endings to the infinitive: \textbf{falarei}, \textbf{falarás}, \textbf{falará}. It is the one you will read.

\section[daqui a]{daqui a — in (so much time from now)}

\label{lesson:PT-C136-daqui-a}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to happen, then the Portuguese for the future.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: daqui a}
\textbf{daqui a} — \textquotedblleft{}in (so much time from now)\textquotedblright{}. Count forward from now: \textbf{daqui a dois dias} — \textquotedblleft{}in two days\textquotedblright{}, \textbf{Daqui a uma semana, vou viajar.} — \textquotedblleft{}In a week I am going to travel.\textquotedblright{}

\section[planear]{planear — to plan}

\label{lesson:PT-C136-planear}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for in, then the Portuguese for a plan.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: planear}
\textbf{planear} — \textquotedblleft{}to plan\textquotedblright{}. Portugal says \textbf{planear}; Brazil says \textbf{planejar}. Like other verbs in \textbf{-ear}, it takes an \textbf{i} where the stress falls: \textbf{eu planeio}. \textbf{Vou planear a viagem.} — \textquotedblleft{}I am going to plan the trip.\textquotedblright{}

\section[organizar]{organizar — to organise}

\label{lesson:PT-C136-organizar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for a plan, then the Portuguese for to plan.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: organizar}
\textbf{organizar} — \textquotedblleft{}to organise\textquotedblright{}. A regular \textbf{-ar} verb, so its one-word future follows \textbf{falar}: \textbf{Organizarei tudo.} — \textquotedblleft{}I will organise everything.\textquotedblright{} In everyday speech: \textbf{Vou organizar tudo.}
